Chapter 9: Parenting, Education, and the Power of Small Changes.
Picture this: sunlight spills across a kitchen floor, and a parent quietly watches their child dive into a pile of toys—blocks, dolls, cars, art supplies, you name it. No one's telling the child what to play with. Instead, there's encouragement to explore. Maybe the child builds a tower, dresses a doll, then sketches a rocket ship. There’s no plan, just genuine curiosity and joy guiding every move.
It’s amazing how much of a difference these little choices can make. When parents and teachers start to notice their own assumptions, suddenly, they’re able to create spaces that welcome every kind of interest and talent.
Think about a teacher who sees that girls aren’t raising their hands as often in math class. Instead of letting that slide, she makes a point to call on them more. Or imagine a parent who notices how much their son loves dance class—and cheers him on, instead of nudging him toward the soccer field.
These shifts don’t have to be dramatic. Most of the time, it’s those small moments—a simple word of praise, an invitation to try something new, or just the patience to really listen—that end up making the biggest impact. And over the years, these moments stack up, shaping a child’s confidence, their skills, and how much they believe in themselves.
In schools, when educators push back against old stereotypes, students start to shine in ways no one expects. Maybe a girl is told she could be an engineer, or a boy is encouraged to write poetry. Those tiny seeds of belief? They grow into something real. Suddenly, the classroom feels like a place where everyone can find their voice.
Most of us don't realize just how much influence we have to shape the world around us. But when we do, the rewards are clear: kids who feel free to be themselves—to explore, to learn, and to grow without limits.
